title: Exchange durable requester tool calls
summary: Register immutable schemas and toolsets, read durable model calls, and post exact requester-owned results through the mailbox.
use_when: An application must expose constrained tools and service or recover their calls across requester restarts.
do_not_use_when: Nucleus is expected to execute domain tools, decide domain success, or invent a missing result.
outcome: A model tool call and its exact requester result are durably correlated and transported.
effects: Schema/toolset registration retains immutable definitions. Calls retain arguments and result posting changes the operational mailbox.
The requester may commit domain mutations after its own validation; Nucleus transports the result to Codex.
authority: Nucleus owns registration identity and mailbox transport.
The requester owns validation, idempotent domain commits, exact result retention, domain success, and retries.
success: The selected call and at most one exact matching requester result are retained; requester state independently proves its domain outcome.
failure_and_recovery: Recover the pending call and requester commit after restart; replay only the exact result and avoid repeating committed domain work.
A terminal owner rejects a new answer; inspect domain effects before any replacement job.
privacy: Nucleus private state can contain complete prompts, source content, tool arguments and results, exact harness output, and terminal diagnostics. Keep state, logs, and backups private.

interfaces.label: Register a toolset
interfaces.invocation: POST /v1/toolsets over the Nucleus Unix socket

interfaces.label: Read calls
interfaces.invocation: GET /v1/jobs/{job}/tool-calls?after=0&waitSeconds=30 over the Nucleus Unix socket

interfaces.label: Post one result
interfaces.invocation: POST /v1/jobs/{job}/tool-calls/{call}/result over the Nucleus Unix socket

interfaces.label: Read a schema
interfaces.invocation: GET /v1/schemas/{schema} over the Nucleus Unix socket

does_not_authorize: Unvalidated domain mutation, an invented tool result, or a new attempt after daemon loss.

consumers.statement: Local requester applications may register immutable tool contracts, read calls, and return their exact validated results.

preconditions.statement: Register the exact immutable schemas/toolset before a job uses them. Persist request correlation and bind each domain commit to a durable exact result.

inputs.statement: Toolset identity is provider/name/version with definitionsSchemaId, definitions and digest. Calls carry job/attempt identity, requestSequence, tool name, arguments schema identity and arguments.
A result supplies version, callId, matching requester identity, resultSchemaId, result, and isError.

outputs.statement: Mailbox reads return versioned calls with retained state, createdAt, and nextSequence; an accepted result is recorded before the blocked Codex call resumes.
Nucleus returns no independent domain-success assertion.

data_semantics.statement: A pending call represents requested work, not a committed result. A schema-bound requester result is transport of the requester's assertion, not Nucleus-authored domain authority.

identity_and_units.statement: Schema IDs and provider/name/version bind immutable registered meaning and digest. Call ID selects one call; requestSequence names its per-attempt stdout atom; createdAt is its retained creation timestamp.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Mailbox reads describe committed local state at the read boundary and can recover a pending call after requester restart. A separate job read is not an atomic snapshot.
No mailbox response-latency or general retention objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One transaction commits the exact item/tool/call stdout observation and pending mailbox projection. The result is retained in the operational mailbox, not copied to reporting storage, before Codex is woken.

Requester identity must match the job. At most one exact result is accepted; identical replay is recoverable and a conflicting result cannot replace it. A new answer is rejected when its job or attempt is terminal.
An absent requester leaves the job waiting_on_requester until cancellation or timeout, retaining its slot. Daemon restart marks unfinished attempts lost and cannot resume the harness process.

operational_limits.statement: Nucleus never runs requester domain tools or retries domain work automatically; one active requester wait holds one of eight slots.
No general mailbox-capacity, database-size, or call-volume bound is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Changed registered meaning requires a new immutable schema/toolset identity or version with historical decoders retained. The transport retains version-one meaning.
No general requester-support or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Dynamic calls and their blocked-call transport rely on the exact adapter-proved Codex app-server behavior; no installed Chancery contract covers it.
